messages:
incident-bot: PAGER -> Maria (SRE-oncall). PrivateConnect DNS blackholing detected in us-east-3. Multiple PrivateLink endpoints returning SERVFAIL/empty responses, connection attempts failing. Severity: P1. Affected customers: acme-corp (prod), beta-saas (staging). PagerDuty: INC-4521. Runbook: privateconnect-dns-failure. Please ACK and start mitigation.

Maria (SRE-oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Starting quick triage now — checking DNS resolvers, edge health, and BGP table snapshots.

Maria (SRE-oncall): First quick checks: our edge DNS qps spiked ~3x for internal names in us-east-3. Upstream recursive responses show high SERVFAIL.

Jon (Net-Eng): Joining. I'm seeing NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL when resolving vpce hostnames from multiple customer VPCs. Running dig from a customer resolver shows no answers: 

```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> vpce-abc123.acme.internal
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0
```

Jon (Net-Eng): traceroutes to the PrivateLink VIPs stop after our egress, packets hit a null next-hop at the partner handoff (hop 3). Looks like route dropped/blackhole on partner side or route suppression.

Ashwin (Cloud-Infra): I see a BGP AS path change from the dedicated partner peer to our DX/DirectConnect partner in us-east-3 at ~1795002300. Their announcements for customer /32s were withdrawn and replaced with a default/blackhole community. Provider status page currently shows no widespread infra alert.

Maria (SRE-oncall): That would explain selective DNS failures + connectivity loss. If the partner removed next-hop or suppressed specific prefixes, our resolvers can fail to reach authoritative reply.

Jon (Net-Eng): Quick mitigation options: 1) Ask partner to re-announce customer prefixes (fastest). 2) Temporarily reroute affected customer traffic via our us-east-1 peering (policy-based failover). 3) Add static DNS records in Redwood Private DNS / customers' private hosted zones to bypass broken resolution until BGP is fixed. 4) If necessary, update frontend routing to the alternate region.

Maria (SRE-oncall): Which is quickest? Partner re-announce is quickest but depends on their ops. Reroute to us-east-1 is possible but requires updating route tables and may impact latency. Static DNS entry could be quickest for control-plane-only impacts.

Luis (Account Support): I've opened a high-priority channel with acme-corp and asked their network team to accept temporary failover. They requested an ETA and control-plane-safe workarounds; they prefer us to do DNS override rather than asking their infra to change anything.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook step 1: Verify customer list -> acme-corp, beta-saas. Step 2: Capture packet captures and traceroutes -> attach to INC-4521. Step 3: If partner route leak suspected, escalate to Partner NOC and request BGP table diff.

Jon (Net-Eng): I'm pushing a scoped policy to the routing control plane to prefer us-east-1 for prefixes 10.200.0.0/22 and 10.201.0.0/24 for affected customers. This will divert egress without touching customer VPC config (should be safe). Command run (internal):

```
# policy push (internal orchestration)
ORCH apply-route-policy --policy "prefer-us-east-1-failover" --prefixes 10.200.0.0/22,10.201.0.0/24 --priority 50
```

Jon (Net-Eng): Policy applied, BGP updates propagating. Trace -> now reaches us-east-1 border instead of getting suppressed.

Maria (SRE-oncall): I'm adding temporary static entries in Redwood Private DNS for acme-corp vpce hostnames so app teams can resolve while we monitor. Please note TTL is low (30s) so we can rollback quickly.

Ashwin (Cloud-Infra): Partner NOC replied: they applied a suppress community during maintenance which inadvertently hit customer /32s, will re-announce in 3–5 mins. They're restoring now and will provide postmortem.

Maria (SRE-oncall): Good. Keep monitoring. I'll keep failover policy in place until partner confirms stable. Check health checks and error rates on edge resolvers.

Jon (Net-Eng): DNS error rate for affected hostnames dropped by 80% since reroute; connection success for acme-corp services returned.

Luis (Account Support): Informed acme-corp that we applied temporary DNS override and traffic failover; they asked to be notified when original path restored.

Ashwin (Cloud-Infra): Partner confirmed re-announce at 1795002660. BGP table shows the original paths are back; removing suppress community. I'll coordinate withdraw of our failover policy after 2 propagation intervals.

Maria (SRE-oncall): Rolling back route policy now to reintroduce normal routing.

Jon (Net-Eng): Policy removed. Verifying that traceroutes now take the original path and DNS resolves from customer resolvers without LEV overrides.

Maria (SRE-oncall): Observability check: DNS SERFAIL rates returned to baseline, latency normal. Marking incident as mitigated. Downgrading severity from P1 -> P2 while we wait for partner postmortem and confirm no residual impact.

Luis (Account Support): Acme-corp acknowledged and is monitoring. They want a full timeline and RCA once we get partner postmortem.

ops-runbook-bot: Incident checklist update: mitigation applied, customers notified, on-call handoff scheduled if needed, create RCA ticket.

Maria (SRE-oncall): Handoff: Ashwin will own partner coordination and RCA. I'm logging actions and will follow up in INC-4521 notes. I'm off shift at 04:30; Ashwin please escalate to SRE manager if there's any regression.

Ashwin (Cloud-Infra): I'll take over and open a ticket with partner NOC for detailed timeline and ask for prevented-change controls. Will add recommended hardening (BGP prefix filters, community safeguards) to the next infra sprint.

Maria (SRE-oncall): Thanks team. Final status: customer-facing impact cleared, temporary DNS override removed, route policy rolled back, partner to deliver postmortem. Closing thread for now — will append RCA link when available. :white_check_mark:
